stem: Looking at a portrait, Deepak says, 'Her father is the only son of my grandfather.' How is the person in the portrait related to Deepak?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Deepak's grandfather's only son = Deepak's father. The portrait person's father is Deepak's father. So the portrait person and Deepak share the same father = they are siblings. The portrait person is female (her), so she is Deepak's sister.
Treating 'only son of my grandfather' as referring to Deepak himself (instead of Deepak's father) places the portrait person one generation below Deepak, giving daughter.
Reversing the chain so that the portrait person is one generation above Deepak gives mother instead of sister.
Treating the shared ancestor as Deepak's brother rather than Deepak's father makes the portrait person a niece, misidentifying the generational link.

explanation: Deepak's grandfather's only son = Deepak's father. The portrait person's father is Deepak's father. Same father, different child = sibling. The portrait person is female (her), so she is Deepak's sister.

explanation_sections.punchline: Grandfather's only son = Deepak's father; sharing that father with the portrait person makes her Deepak's sister.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply most-certain first: 'grandfather's only son' uniquely identifies Deepak's father. The portrait person's father is that same man. Common father = siblings. Pronoun 'her' confirms the portrait person is female = sister.
explanation_sections.lesson: When a portrait or photo description pins the subject's parent as someone already in your tree, the subject is your sibling (if parent is same-generation) or cousin (if one generation over).
explanation_sections.timing: Under 80 s. Primary trap: option 2 (daughter) from reading 'only son' as Deepak himself.
